title: PresentNullPositions
description: Issue #110: the positions where the schema PERMITS a null, which is the other half of explicit_null_positions.json. A null there is not refused, so it survives the decode as the nil pointer, nil collection or untouched zero an ABSENT property also leaves -- and both halves of that are wrong. It was dropped on the way out, and any keyword the property states was then measured against a zero the document never supplied.

untyped.$comment: The empty schema. Permits every value including null, and states nothing, so nothing rejects the null and nothing but the record says it was there.

boundOnly.$comment: A constraint and no type. minLength is vacuous for a null, but the optional rule is gated on key presence -- which a present null satisfies -- so it used to read the Go zero and reject the document for a length of 0. That is the false rejection, and it is the whole document under --omit-empty=false.

reqBoundOnly.$comment: The same, required. There is no presence guard at all on a required property's rules, so the zero was read whatever the flags said.

nullableScalar.$comment: The idiomatic nullable spelling. omitempty used to be suppressed here so that nil marshalled as null -- which kept a present null and invented one for an absent property. Now the null is recorded and the tag says what it should about absence.

nullableList.$comment: The same for a collection: a nil slice is a null, a present [] is an empty array, and an absent property is neither.

nullableObject.$comment: A property whose type carries its own Validate. Under --omit-empty=false the field is a struct value rather than a pointer, so encoding/json hands the null to its UnmarshalJSON and the zero struct then reaches Validate -- where the required key it does not have is a rejection of a document the schema permits. The required key is what makes that visible.

refObject.$comment: A property whose type carries its own Validate and, under --omit-empty=false, is held by value rather than behind a pointer.

refList.$comment: The case the field-type Validate has to be kept away from. A null leaves a nil slice, which is also what an absent property leaves and what an empty array is not -- and the named type's own Validate reads that nil as an array of length 0 and reports it short of minItems. The schema permits the null, so that is a rejection of a conforming document, and NullGuard is what stops the call being made.

typedString.$comment: The accept-control: a property whose schema FORBIDS null keeps issue #103's refusal and must not be tracked here. Exactly one of the two paths claims each property.
